criteria.rationale: Material assumptions: Git skips a refresh whose lock cannot be made and trusts stat only for files older than the index. Tests and probes verified both on this Linux Git. L2 is accepted; /proc availability, Git 2.31 or newer and non-Linux runtime stay unverified.
No command, flag, record or MCP schema changes. Probes show the diffs answer as the plain diff, including missing and symlinked index and range bases.

The cause is a stat refresh written under .git. Optional locks cover status (R1) and the diff reads an unlockable memfd that keeps the index time (D1); D2 justifies testing the reads. The end-to-end probe left the index unchanged. The design delta has no structural deltas to map.
No command, flag or template changes. The spec's execution log and follow-ups match the round 4 code.
Index errors name the repository and failure, and scope selection carries the cause. The silent skip in check is low and tracked in N18.
The ten subject code files match the spec's artifact list; round 4 changes only the index read. artifact-check --strict exited 0.

The bound now applies to the bytes read from one open file, the redirecting Git environment stays stripped, and the memfd creates no file. The FIFO block needs local .git write access and is low, tracked in N21.

Locks alone do not stop git diff writing and a temporary copy creates files, so an unlockable memfd over the unchanged diff is the smallest sufficient approach found. It becomes invalid if Git stops skipping a failed refresh lock or /proc is unavailable.
